transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’m tired all the time. Not just normal teacher-at-the-end-of-the-day tired—like, even after a full night’s sleep, I have to push myself through grading, dinner, and getting ready for the next morning.
Outside of feeling so tired, have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Most days, yes. I can still smile for my students and get through the lessons, but underneath I feel kind of gray and flat. Then I get home and even things I usually like, like my garden or watercolors, just feel far away.
About how long have you been feeling this way?
About two years now—two years and a couple months. It started around when my husband stopped working outside the home and our routine at home changed.
During these past two years, has there been any period of two months or more where you felt back to your usual self?
No, I don’t think so. It’s been pretty steady for the whole two years and two months, since our routine changed when my husband stopped working outside the home.
Before this started two years ago, did you ever experience any other periods in your life when you felt down or depressed?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time that stands out like this.
How has your self-esteem or the way you feel about yourself been over these past two years?

I’ve been pretty hard on myself. I keep thinking I should be handling everything better. If my lesson plans take twice as long, or I have to say no to mentoring a newer teacher, I tell myself I’m letting my family and my school down.
Over these past two years, have you found yourself feeling hopeless about the future?

I don’t feel like everything is falling apart, exactly. But I have a hard time believing I’m going to feel lighter again, or get back to being the person who looked forward to museums, projects, and quiet afternoons.
During this time, have you had any thoughts of death or wishing you wouldn't wake up?
No. I haven’t had thoughts about dying or not waking up.
